- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction to bearish signals.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves after recent spikes — model tends to overcorrect; apply lagged mean reversion for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward trend, cap forecast decline to avoid premature bearish reversal.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misreads momentum — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth out false signals.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially >10% above recent peak) should be capped at 5–7% below true peak to avoid overbought bias.  
- When sentiment is consistently low and price is trending down, model often underestimates support — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid bottoming too early.
